target_claim: ActiveForcing performs online physical adaptation on top of a frozen pretrained VLA, without retraining the VLA.
scope: Starting from a common established-grasp state; physical probing and force selection occur online. Frozen VLA generates arm actions under native50-step prediction/10-step execution schedule. AF controls squeeze; VLA open intent is preserved.
feasibility_training_disclosure: Existing647 supervision rows came from controlled scripted-motion full-task outcomes. The current64D model exactly removes seven constant phase columns and is transferred without fitting new weights. VLA transfer is verified separately using online development and final fresh-root rollouts. Never label the647 rows as VLA-matched training data.
chunk_conditioning_disclosure: Current initial online VLA chunk supplies six kinematic channels. These channels had negligible motion variation in old647 data; do not claim that varied VLA motion effects were learned from that training corpus. Report observed input-range extrapolation and empirical transfer.
force_adaptation_schedule: One posterior-aware force setpoint is chosen after the probe using the current predicted chunk; unchanged force controller regulates it throughout grasp execution. No claim of posterior/F replanning at every VLA chunk.
observability_disclosure: Current simulator-state object velocity is an online input; real-robot perception availability is not established. No hidden material friction is read during deployment selection.
success_and_drop: Report frozen geometric full-task success and independently measured pre-release drops separately. Any recovered-drop geometric success must be disclosed.
statistics: Four fresh root groups; paired contexts and shared policy-noise seeds. Do not count192 branches as192 independent roots.
scripted_results_role: Controlled-motion engineering evidence only; excluded from all online-VLA main and ablation outcomes.
methodological_limitations_not_removed_b: One burned root for transfer qualification
Native online inference in simulation is not a real-robot hard-real-time claim
